quotes.text:
Today at 2:15 PM ET I’ll be teaming up with @SafeHousePrjct to unveil Simply Report, the first survivor-informed AI powered app that sends anonymous trafficking tips straight to law enforcement and connects survivors to critical care. 

Tune in here: https://t.co/8eZXOwS6ws

Since coming to Congress, I’ve said we need to win the economics of conflict. 

Today in @HouseScience, I pressed Google Quantum AI on how quantum tech can do that. 

Their response? Defense stands to gain first—with better intel and stronger protection for our warfighters. https://t.co/Bi92twsxTK

@FiveMinWithMike FPVs can be controlled by fiber optic cable, a technique currently being employed by both Russia and Ukraine. Targeting can also be AI driven. Both are impervious to electronic countermeasures/jamming.

It was great to attend @tedxcatawba this weekend in Hickory. From cutting-edge AI to national security, law, and leadership, every speaker brought something real to the table. 

It’s exciting to see this kind of innovation in the heart of NC! https://t.co/YV1vGjKhFl

The AI race is the new space race, and @POTUS just committed $90 billion to it through major investments in AI and energy. 

He is sending a clear message to China that American leadership in critical technology is back. https://t.co/fatVzwhj2I

7. Using AI to speed up military construction.
 Base projects are stuck in bureaucratic bottlenecks, AI helps streamline planning and approvals.

AI is the next great arena of American power, and the stakes couldn’t be higher.

The Trump administration’s AI Action Plan unleashes our labs, cuts the red tape, and puts American innovation in the driver’s seat to win the 21st century. https://t.co/HQ680l7NdK

The One Big Beautiful Bill puts $450 million toward using AI in Navy shipbuilding:

⚠️ U.S. warships are delayed by years and billions over budget ⚠️ China builds more ships in a year than we’ve built since WWII ⚠️ Our fleet is shrinking as our adversarial threats are growing

AI is how we speed up production, close the gap, and keep our @USNavy ahead.

America has four strategic advantages that make us the world's foremost superpower: food production, energy dominance, military strength, and AI leadership. 

Two of those advantages depend directly on nuclear power—cheap, ubiquitous energy and artificial intelligence. 

If we want to maintain our position in the world, we have to get serious about nuclear energy.

.@POTUS absolutely made the right call blocking Nvidia's request to sell advanced AI chips to China.

Giving our biggest adversary access to cutting-edge American AI technology would hand them the tools to surpass us in military systems, surveillance, and autonomous weapons. 

National security comes before corporate profits, and this administration understands that.

.@POTUS is exactly right. We're in a computing arms race with China that will define the next century, and whoever leads in AI and advanced manufacturing will have decisive economic and military advantages. 

China knows this and they're racing to catch up, which is why we need to keep building, keep investing, and maintain our lead in the technologies that will shape our future.

I spoke this afternoon at the 6th Energy Innovation & AI Forum, where leaders across government and industry met off the record to talk honestly about the future of American power. AI demand is skyrocketing, and every sector that matters—defense, manufacturing, research, and infrastructure—is about to rely on far more energy than our grid can deliver.

I made the case that if America wants to stay ahead, we need to build: more natural gas capacity, next-generation nuclear, stronger transmission, and a permitting system that can keep up with innovation.

If there is a hybridized version that provides reasonable individual liberty protections but also provides certainty to those who are innovating with massive investments but also impact the future of our market economy, that would be interesting. We have to step back and think from a national security standpoint and see that our adversaries are not going to constrain AI. We should offer a limited period of time where we constrain it within limitations; that will help our national security. This is one of the key areas we lead in. I would be okay with that.

We need to allow energy to be produced rapidly in our country. I’m a nuclear guy. Regulation is too heavy there. I introduced NDAA legislation that allows public-private partnerships that allow for that to be generated on military bases and it allows us to pipe power outside of the military base. This also helps data centers without taking power from current localities.

As I told @NBCNews, Operation Epic Fury, where our warfighters struck over 2,000 targets with remarkable precision, showed exactly what AI can do when paired with the irreplaceable judgment and experience of the American warfighter. 

The question is never whether to put these tools in their hands, it is whether we are moving fast enough to stay ahead of China and Russia.

Every major scientific domain, every top national laboratory, the world's best supercomputers, and the private sector all working together through AI to transform how America innovates. 

That is the Genesis Mission and that is how we stay ahead of China. 

The countries that win the AI race will set the terms for global power for decades to come and this administration is making sure that country is the United States.
https://t.co/zdnR45WPc7

.@BernieSanders is hosting a panel this Wednesday with a professor from Tsinghua University, one of China's top universities with direct ties to the Chinese Communist Party, and Zeng Yi, the Dean of the Beijing Institute of AI Safety and Governance, to argue that America needs to work with China on AI policy.

This is the same China that just blocked Meta's $2 billion deal to acquire Manus AI, a startup whose founders had already moved to Singapore and whose deal was already done and closed. Beijing decided it did not matter. They stepped in, killed the deal, and restricted the founders from leaving the country while it was under review.

China is aggressively locking down their most powerful AI assets and shutting American companies out. Bernie Sanders wants to hand them a seat at the table to help decide how America handles the same technology. Make that make sense.

We are in a race with China to dominate AI, and American companies need to be on America's side. 

Helping Chinese startups access cutting edge technology while simultaneously holding major US government contracts is not a both sides issue. Pick a lane. https://t.co/fkWXjs7Cg8

Last night, an unmanned drone boat found two of our pilots floating in the waters off Oman and brought them home, marking the first time the U.S. has ever used an autonomous vessel for a real world rescue. 

That happened because we made the decision years ago to invest in this technology, and kept investing even when the results weren’t visible yet.

China has already made that same bet at scale, with urgency, and without a doubt about whether it's worth it. Whoever wins the AI race controls how wars are fought, how fast decisions get made, and whether you can project power anywhere on earth without putting a crew in harm's way.

Last night was a glimpse of what winning looks like.

Most people saw a rescue, but I saw a weapons system, and a reminder of exactly how far behind we can't afford to fall.

The AI arms race is no longer between companies, it is between nations, and China is treating it that way. 

If Beijing becomes the global hub for AI infrastructure, the consequences for American national security and economic competitiveness will be permanent. https://t.co/nghokQFfEh

The most alarming part of this story isn't that Microsoft is looking for a cheaper AI model, it's that a Chinese model is even in the conversation.

For years, we've been told the United States is in a strategic competition with China for leadership in artificial intelligence. If that's true, America's biggest technology companies should be helping widen that gap, not looking for ways to close it.
https://t.co/eEz8KUrPoB

What happens when AI, American manufacturing, and millions of American families all depend on the same electric grid? 

That's the energy challenge we're heading into, and it's exactly why the House passed my bipartisan legislation to accelerate next-generation geothermal.
https://t.co/yABiVwfAlL

The AI race, the manufacturing resurgence, and America's energy future all run through the electric grid.

To meet that challenge, I introduced the Lowering Energy Costs through Grid Modernization Act to expand grid capacity, strengthen reliability, and lower energy costs using the infrastructure we already have. 
https://t.co/IlSqXWiARw

The Chinese Communist Party has made a national strategy out of closing the gap by acquiring technologies it didn’t invent. 

If the United States is serious about winning the AI race, protecting American innovation must become a core national security priority. 

We cannot allow the technologies that secure our future to become the foundation of China’s rise.

Congress can't fix our defense acquisition system without hearing directly from the people trying to navigate it. 

It was great visiting Airship AI in Mooresville to discuss AI, acquisition reform, and how we can make sure innovative American companies spend more time building technology and less time fighting bureaucracy.

AI is beginning to play a role not just in solving problems, but in building the next generation of AI itself, and we need to understand what that means before the technology outruns our ability to measure it. I’m proud to co-lead the Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act to give NIST the visibility it needs to track these capabilities as they develop.

For most of AI’s history, humans have been the ones making it smarter. Now, AI is starting to help do that work too, and we need to know how quickly that balance is changing.

My bipartisan Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act has @NIST track how much AI is contributing to AI research, how much still requires humans, and how fast that gap is closing.
https://t.co/xsCAgriv1E

AI is moving incredibly fast, and we need a clear picture of what the most advanced systems can actually do. As AI begins taking on more of the work involved in developing the next generation of AI, the pace of progress could accelerate dramatically. This bill makes sure we can track those developments without putting new mandates on American companies or getting in the way of innovation.

If you steal 2,000 pages of American AI secrets and try to hand China the keys to our technological advantage, you should spend a long time in prison.

This guy is exactly why I introduced the FAFO Act. Spy for China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea, and 10 years behind bars should be the floor, not the ceiling.

I’m taking this on in Congress, @sama! 

I’ll be introducing legislation soon to help the people who run our power grid and other critical systems use AI to stop cyberattacks before they cause real damage. https://t.co/7Nl8RVGbYK

A cyberattack on our power grid, hospitals, or water systems can have real consequences for millions of Americans.

I’ll be introducing the NIST Defensive Standards Act to make sure the companies building our best AI are working directly with the people protecting those systems to find weaknesses and stop attacks before they happen.

I introduced the Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act for one reason: as AI races ahead, we need to understand how it affects the American people, what it can do, where it’s going, and how our adversaries are keeping pace. https://t.co/kmqHNZ7Pvw

Some of the greatest advances in artificial intelligence are happening right here in America, and we have a responsibility to make sure that technology is secure. Our adversaries are already looking for ways to exploit these systems, and as AI becomes more powerful, the risks to our critical infrastructure will only grow. We need to get the companies developing this technology working directly with the people responsible for defending our power grids, hospitals, and financial systems.

“Our adversaries just see it as much more beneficial” to let American companies do the expensive work of advancing AI while they steal the results.

My bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act takes that threat head-on, directing @NIST to develop standards to protect American AI breakthroughs from foreign theft and strengthen the cyber defenses of the critical infrastructure our country depends on.

One of my concerns is that our adversaries just see it as much more beneficial and productive for them as this [U.S. industry] engine burns,” said Harrigan. “Where they actually just see it as more beneficial for themselves in the short term, to hang six to 12 months behind the United States, let us burn really hot and for 5 to 10% of the spend, they can just distill and steal, and they can do that up to until the point where our market kind of falters. At which point they can turn it into high gear, having not expended those resources yet in the past, and actually leapfrog us.

My bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act is getting international attention, and for good reason.

America cannot afford to lead the world in AI only to hand our adversaries the tools to attack our own critical infrastructure.
https://t.co/agXTCRyRq5

⏱️ TWO MINUTE TOWN HALL

What happens when our adversaries can copy billions of dollars' worth of American technology without paying to develop it themselves?

This week, we're talking about that threat, what AI-powered cyberattacks could mean for our hospitals and power grids, and how my bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act takes on both problems.
